profile.reading:
This facility at 8949 Sorensen Parkway in the Irvington area of north Omaha, Nebraska, carries the name of Jack Koraleski, a longtime Union Pacific executive who rose through the company's marketing and sales organization to serve as vice chairman before being named chief executive officer, a position he held until his retirement in 2015. Koraleski was later inducted into the University of Nebraska Omaha business hall of fame in recognition of his career at the railroad. Naming a major operational or technology building after a former senior executive is a common practice among large, long established railroads, and Union Pacific has followed that pattern here.

Union Pacific Railroad, together with its parent Union Pacific Corporation, is one of North America's largest Class I freight railroads, moving agricultural, industrial, energy, and intermodal freight across a network spanning the western two thirds of the United States. The company's corporate headquarters sits downtown at Union Pacific Center, a 317 foot office tower at 1400 Douglas Street that opened in June 2004. This Sorensen Parkway address, several miles north of downtown near Omaha's Eppley Airfield, is a separate location from that headquarters tower, consistent with a dedicated technology or research building rather than general office space.

Large freight railroads depend on extensive, continuously available information technology to run functions such as train dispatching and network scheduling, shipment tracking, safety systems including federally mandated positive train control, and customer facing logistics platforms, all of which require reliable data center capacity somewhere in the company's real estate footprint. It is reasonable to expect a building carrying a technology and research and development designation, bearing a former CEO's name, and located apart from the main headquarters to serve some part of that function for Union Pacific's own operations. However, Union Pacific has not published a facility description, opening date, capacity figure, or specific account of what research or technology work takes place inside this particular building, so its exact role within the company's broader technology infrastructure is not something that can be confirmed from public materials, only inferred from the company's operational needs and the building's name and location.

reading:
Union Pacific Railroad is a Class I freight railroad headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Its single row in this registry corresponds to a building the county confirms the railroad owns, though the classification of that building as a data centre rests on a much thinner foundation than the ownership does.

The Douglas County 2026 Board of Equalization parcel record settles the property facts. PIN 1418100700 has a property address of 8949 Sorensen Parkway in the 68122 postal area, and is recorded as lying in unincorporated Douglas County rather than within the City of Omaha. The legal description is Irvington Technology Park, Lot 1, Block 0, covering 20.051 acres. The owner of record is Union Pacific Railroad, with an owner mailing address of 1400 Douglas Street, Stop 1640, which is the railroad's downtown headquarters. The parcel carries one building of 53,646 square feet, single storey, built in 2002, with a county building description of light manufacturing industrial and both quality and condition recorded as good. It falls in the Omaha Public Schools district and the Irvington fire district. The account type is state assessed railroad property, which is why both land and total value appear as zero on the county roll, railroad property in Nebraska being centrally assessed by the state rather than locally.

This corrects an earlier reading of the record. The facility is not part of Union Pacific Center at 1400 Douglas Street in downtown Omaha. That address appears on the parcel only as the owner's mailing address, and the property itself lies several miles to the north west of it.

The mapping history explains where the rest of the record came from. The building polygon was created on 7 June 2012 and refreshed on 2 April 2016 from Bing imagery, and on both occasions was named First Data Resources Inc, with the Sorensen Parkway address tags that survive to this day. On 14 June 2025 a contributor renamed it to Union Pacific Jack Koraleski Technology, Research and Development Center and added the data centre telecom tag, then a minute later added the operator tag and a Wikidata reference for Union Pacific Railroad in a changeset commented simply as adding an operator to a building.

So the change of ownership is corroborated by the county, but the computing function is not corroborated by anything. No published source describes what happens inside the building, and no IT load, utility service, standby diesel generation or on site generation figure exists for it in any record found here. John J Koraleski was a Union Pacific executive elected to its board in July 2012 who later served as chief executive, and naming a technology building after a former senior officer is ordinary railroad practice, but a name is not evidence of a data hall. A 53,646 square foot single storey light industrial building on 20 acres could equally house laboratories, training space or offices, and this registry should record only what the county establishes.
